title: Geometric Čech coface of normalized singleton tensor sections
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], F a quasi-coherent X-module [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module], U and W étale X-objects, and g:W→U. Put A=Γ(U,O), B=Γ(W,O), and M=Γ(U,U*F). In degrees n and n+1 let f and f' be homomorphisms from the lifted tensor modules M tensor_A B^{tensor(n+1)} and M tensor_A B^{tensor(n+2)} to the singleton tensor-section Čech terms. Assume both maps have the pure-tensor normalization [new-etale-affine-singleton-tensor-degree-comparison-hom-normalization]: evaluation at the unique outer tuple is the product of the projection pullbacks of b(k), acting on the restriction of m from U. For every j∈Fin(n+2), m∈M, and b:Fin(n+1)→B, the geometric Čech coface δ_j sends f(ULift(m tensor tprod(b))) to f'(ULift(m tensor tprod(j.insertNth 1 b))). Neither f nor f' is assumed invertible. No assertion about the Amitsur coface map is made.

source.place: Tag 03P2, Theorem 59.22.4, affine singleton Čech/Amitsur identification; Tag 03DR, equation 35.8.0.1

proof.text: Let P and Q be the categorical products of n+1 and n+2 copies of W→U. The product map p:Q→P omits j, and p followed by the k-th projection is the j.succAbove(k)-th projection, by Pi.lift_π. The formal-coproduct Čech face has index map precomposition with j.succAbove and component p. Its presheaf map is a product lift of projection followed by section restriction. Evaluating at the constant-zero tuple uses Pi.lift_π and gives restriction along p of the evaluated input section.

Apply hf to the input m tensor tprod(b). By the semilinearity clause of the restriction theorem, restricting this section pulls back the product of projection functions as a scalar, and restricts the coefficient section. The composition clause and p's over-U triangle identify the restricted coefficient with direct restriction from U to Q. Ring-map preservation of products and p's projection equations identify the scalar with the product of the retained Q-projection functions.

Apply hf' to m tensor tprod(j.insertNth 1 b). Its evaluated scalar product has j-th factor the pullback of 1, hence 1. Fin.prod_univ_succAbove and insertNth at j.succAbove identify the other factors with those in the preceding step. Thus evaluated outputs agree. The outer product index Fin(n+2)→Fin1 is a singleton, so its projection is the hom of productUniqueIso and is injective. ULift.down is injective too. Therefore the Čech coface of f's pure value is f' of the inserted-unit pure value. When n=0 there are the two usual projection restrictions; zero section groups obey the same equations.

lean.statement:
theorem singletonTensorCech_normalized_coface
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (U W : X.Etale) (g : W ⟶ U) (n : ℕ) (j : Fin (n + 2))
    (f : (singletonTensorAmitsur X F U W g).X n ⟶
      (singletonTensorCech X F U W g).X n)
    (f' : (singletonTensorAmitsur X F U W g).X (n + 1) ⟶
      (singletonTensorCech X F U W g).X (n + 1))
    (hf : IsSingletonTensorDegreeComparisonHom X F U W g n f)
    (hf' : IsSingletonTensorDegreeComparisonHom X F U W g (n + 1) f')
    (m : Γ((Modules.tensorPullback U.hom).obj F, ⊤))
    (b : Fin (n + 1) → Γ(W.left, ⊤)) :
    letI : Algebra Γ(U.left, ⊤) Γ(W.left, ⊤) := g.left.appTop.hom.toAlgebra
    (singletonTensorCechCosimplicial X F U W g).δ j
      (f (ULift.up (m ⊗ₜ[Γ(U.left, ⊤)] PiTensorProduct.tprod Γ(U.left, ⊤) b))) =
    f' (ULift.up (m ⊗ₜ[Γ(U.left, ⊤)]
      PiTensorProduct.tprod Γ(U.left, ⊤) (j.insertNth 1 b)))
